The first public release of the DexTor OS for Windows launcher - and the first time its full
source code is published.

## What it does

- Turns a USB drive of 8 GB or more into a DexTor OS drive that boots on a compatible PC and
  also runs inside Windows 11, in its own window.
- Checks this PC first and changes nothing while checking: Windows version, memory, disk space
  and virtualization.
- Downloads the latest DexTor OS image and resumes interrupted downloads. Before anything is
  written, it verifies the signature of the published SHA-256 with its release key and checks the
  image against that hash.
- Asks before erasing, showing the drive letter, model and size. Refuses system, boot, read-only
  and non-USB disks.
- Writes the image without the Windows cache, then reads it back from the stick and verifies it
  before the drive is marked ready.
- Starts DexTor OS inside Windows on a pinned, verified QEMU with the Windows Hypervisor Platform,
  sized to the computer. The boot is shown as steps behind a DexTor splash, and the window opens
  full screen at the monitor's own resolution once the desktop is ready.
- Gives DexTor OS one private `data.img` on the stick in both modes, for its LUKS-encrypted
  storage, and never runs two DexTor sessions on the same storage at once.
- Speaks 10 languages and hands the selected one to DexTor OS.

## Download

`DexTorOS-Portable-0.1.39-win-x64.exe` - one portable file, no installation and no separate .NET
needed. Requires Windows 11 x64. It was built from exactly the source code of this release
with `build-portable.bat 0.1.39` and .NET SDK 10.0.401.

This is a beta build and it is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns about an
unknown publisher. Check the file before running it:

SHA-256: `D30C493EEC5AA739574E689FFE1F55E41C176BF69716F78A0437A8D05B50F88E`

Third-party components and their licenses: `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, attached to this release.
